title: The Tall tree by the gate
subtitle: 森林生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）
meta: 主题语境：森林生态（自然生态·森林与生态）　|　核心词汇：tall　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tall 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the director wrote of ① a tall tree by the gate in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② taller than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the tall ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the tallest tree by the gate anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too tall to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the tall ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a tall boy in the back row, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as tall as the boy in the back row they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was tall or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something tall, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite tall; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the tall ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another tall tree by the gate in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ taller than anybody had expected. ⑩ The tallest boy in the back row in the whole theatre, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the tall ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 高（前置定语 a tall tree by the gate：1981 年导演在戏报里记下的那件高的树）
B. adj. 高／高大（比较级 taller than：文中两处，一处比门边高大的树，一处比预想）
C. adj. 高／高大（最高级 the tallest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 高（表语 too tall to do：母亲觉得它太高，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 高大（前置定语 a tall boy in the back row：叔叔把整件事称作一桩高大的男孩）
F. adj. 高大（同级比较 as tall as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩后排高个子的男孩相比）
G. adj. 高大（后置定语 something tall：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 高大（受程度副词修饰 quite tall：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a tall tree by the gate
the tallest tree by the gate anybody
a tall boy in the back row
The tallest boy in the back row in

answers.why: tall 意为“高”，1981 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件高的树”，此处作前置定语 a tall tree by the gate。
tall 意为“高”，此处用比较级 taller than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
tall 意为“高”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最高的一件，故用最高级 the tallest tree by the gate。
tall 意为“高”，母亲认为这件东西“太高了，谁也用不上”，too tall to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
tall 意为“高大”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩高大的男孩”，此处作前置定语 a tall boy in the back row。
tall 意为“高大”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩后排高个子的男孩一样高大”，同级比较用 as tall as。
tall 意为“高大”，戏报上那半行字要的是“高大的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something tall。
tall 意为“高大”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当高大”，quite 修饰原级 tall。
tall 意为“高大”，1991 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要高大”，故用比较级 taller than。
tall 意为“高大”，母亲 1993 年说的是“整个戏院里最高大的那一桩”，故用最高级 the tallest boy in the back row。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1981 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件高的树。（a tall tree by the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更高。（taller than …）
母亲觉得它太高，谁也用不上。（too tall to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩高大的男孩。（a tall boy in the back row）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩后排高个子的男孩一样高大。（as tall as …）
到了 1988 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件高大的东西。（something tall）
answers: In 1981 the director wrote of a tall tree by the gate in the poster.
Everybody said it was taller than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too tall to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a tall boy in the back row.
He said nobody would call it as tall as the boy in the back row they had once had.
By 1988 the poster asked for nothing but something tall.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tall 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1981 the director wrote of a tall tree by the gate in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the tallest tree by the gate in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too tall to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a tall boy in the back row, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite tall, and everybody laughed.
The tall ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
